name: Hampton Roads Crossing
researcher_notes: Not an existing row: the only Virginia Natural Gas row is P5990, the cancelled VNG Interconnect, a different project. The Hampton Roads Crossing links the Hampton and Newport News side to the Portsmouth and Norfolk side under Hampton Roads harbor. A May 2008 Virginia Natural Gas groundbreaking release gives about 22 miles total (16 onshore, 5 marine, drilled), 100,000 dekatherms per day of added capacity and an estimated cost of 123 million dollars. A 2013 pipe supplier release confirms 22 miles and 24-inch pipe. A Virginia Places page says the crossing joined the utility's two networks in 2010 and that it is intrastate. Transmission call: it is a 24-inch high-pressure steel line that ties the Columbia Gas Transmission-fed south side to the Dominion-fed Peninsula side, but the sponsor describes it as feeding its distribution system. Judgment call, flag for review. Length rule met (22 mi, over 15.5 mi). Start year not staged: the 2008 release slated late 2009 and the Virginia Places page says 2010; no source states the in-service date firmly. Cost is the 2008 estimate. The Virginia Places page does not give a numeric status, so the Status ref only supports in-service. Owner matched the existing Virginia Natural Gas entity; parent Southern Co as on P5990. No route found in a public GIS source. Tier medium: the press release, the pipe supplier and the Virginia Places page agree, but the supplier release and the Virginia Places page trace back to the same company announcements, so independence is partial.
